summary: A single billing cycle includes ordinary card use that stays within the credit limit, followed by statement closing and a full payment made before the due date. The scenario probes the on-time path where the minimum-payment obligation is satisfied in full and neither a late fee nor an over-limit fee should arise.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of the billing cycle, so the statement's New Balance is determined solely by the cycle's listed transactions.
The cardholder's credit limit is $1000.00, and total posted usage in the cycle never exceeds that limit.
The statement for this cycle shows a New Balance of $300.00, making the contractual minimum payment $15.00 because 3% of $300.00 is $9.00 and the agreement uses the greater of 3% or $15.00.
The payment is received and credited on the same date it is made, and that date is on or before the due date.
This on-time full-payment archetype does not include any returned payment, late payment, or over-limit condition, so no penalty-fee clauses are triggered.
